chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a slave girl, so he freed her, and she married, and gave birth. Is it permissible for her former master to marry her daughter? He (peace be upon him) said: She is prohibited to him, and she is his daughter, and the free woman and the slave girl are equal in this.
And your step-daughters who are in your guardianship, (born) of your wives.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (peace be upon them), similar to it.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of the slave girl he freed and who married someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific mechanism of 'marriage by conjunction' (jam' bayna al-akhawayn) where a freed slave girl becomes the daughter of her former master, rendering her daughter forbidden to him. The Imam cites the verse regarding 'stepdaughters in your charge' to establish that the bond of adoption through manumission creates a permanent mahram relationship, applicable equally to both free and enslaved women. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that manumission creates a quasi-filial link, preventing the master from marrying the freed slave's daughter.
